data.description:
## Context

Discovered while fixing `b2ff-2588-9bb7-4bd2` (change 2662), which closed the
empty-string hole for the BOOLEAN class by making `_as_bool("")` raise. That fix covers
all 27 boolean config keys. AC5 of that bug asked for one pass over ALL config keys for
other places `""` resolves in an unsafe direction. This ticket carries the residue.

## Post-fix sweep: `""` through every coercer in `_config_sections._SECTIONS`

67 of 104 keys now RAISE on `""` — every bool, int, float, `_as_choice`, `_as_git_ref`,
`_as_git_remote`, `_as_tracker_dir`. Those are done. 37 keys still accept it:

- **27 `_as_str` keys -> `""`**
- **7 `_as_str_tuple` keys -> `()`**
- **2 `_as_str_list` keys -> `[]`** (`code_health.scan_roots`, `include_extensions`)
- **1 with a literal fallback** (`ticket.display_mode` -> `"auto"`)

## Already safe — verified at the CONSUMER, not assumed

- `mcp.http_allowed_hosts` / `http_allowed_origins`: an empty allowlist on a
  non-loopback bind raises `McpStartupError` (`mcp_server.py` ~:518). Fails closed.
- `mcp.auth_jwt_algorithms`: empty raises `AuthConfigError`
  (`_mcp_auth.py:265`). Fails closed.
- `jira.url` / `jira.user` / `jira.project` / `reconciler.base_url`: empty leaves the
  integration unconfigured, so operations fail rather than proceed.
- `reconciler.ca_bundle`: empty = system trust store, not a relaxation.

## The residue that needs a disposition

These are keys where an env `""` DEFEATS a file-set value in the protection direction.
Each is a "the operator configured a control, an expanded-to-nothing `${VAR}` removed
it" shape — the same mechanism as the original bug:

- `verify.require_environment` — empty = op-cert environment binding OFF
- `verify.opcert_enforce_since` — empty = no enforcement floor
- `identity.enforce_since` — empty = no identity enforcement floor
- `mcp.auth_required_scopes` — empty tuple -> `required_scopes=None`
  (`mcp_server.py:577`), i.e. no scope requirement
- `mcp.auth_jwt_expected_typ` — empty = no `typ` header check

## Why this is NOT just "make `_as_str` raise on empty"

For several of these keys `""` is the DOCUMENTED "off"/unset spelling and equals the
built-in default (`verify.require_environment` is empty in the committed `rebar.toml`),
so a blanket raise would break the normal configuration. The boolean fix worked because
`""` was never a legitimate boolean; that argument does not transfer. The likely correct
shape is a per-key declaration of whether empty is MEANINGFUL or a FAULT, applied in the
env layer rather than in the coercer.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each of the five listed keys gets an explicit disposition: empty is meaningful
      (documented) or empty is a fault (raises).
- [ ] Whatever mechanism is chosen is declarative per key, not a blanket rule over
      `_as_str` / `_as_str_tuple` — a blanket rule breaks the documented empty defaults.
- [ ] A regression test drives the real resolver with `""` against a file setting the
      opposite for every key whose disposition is "fault", and pins the "meaningful"
      ones as still accepting empty.
- [ ] The already-safe keys above keep their current consumer-side fail-closed
      behaviour; the fix must not move that check out of the consumer.
data.title: Empty-string env overrides still defeat file-set values on five string/tuple config keys (the non-boolean residue of b2ff)
